wu: Warm-up: 'Earth Day Quiz Relay' - Teams race to answer 5 quick questions about Earth Day (e.g., 'When is Earth Day?', 'What does recycle mean?') using flashcards. Winners get 1 point per correct answer.
wuAlt: Alternative 1: 'Green Pictionary' - Students draw Earth Day words (e.g., 'tree', 'water') for teams to guess.
Alternative 2: 'Word Association Chain' - Start with 'Earth', each student adds one related word.
pres: Present 'must/should' for rules using flashcards showing green actions (e.g., 'turn off lights'). Model: 'You must recycle bottles.' 'You should use a reusable bag.' Check understanding with thumbs-up/down.
presAlt: Alternative 1: Use a short story about a student who doesn't follow green rules, then correct with must/should.
Alternative 2: Show a video clip of littering, discuss what people must/should do.
prac: Guided practice: 'Green Rules Sorting' - Teams sort 10 picture cards into 'must' (e.g., 'save water') and 'should' (e.g., 'plant trees') categories. Monitor and correct errors.
pracAlt: Alternative 1: 'Sentence Builder' - Students match halves of sentences (e.g., 'You must...' + 'not waste food').
Alternative 2: 'Rule Relay' - Teams write one must/should rule per student on the board.
ls: Listening slot: 'Earth Day Tips' - Students listen to a short audio (3 tips) and match them to pictures. Check with peer correction.
re: Reactivation game: 'Green Charades' - Students act out green actions (e.g., 'compost') for teams to shout the verb form ('You must compost!').
prod: Production task: 'Eco-Poster Campaign' - Teams design a 5-rule poster for the American Space using must/should (e.g., 'You must use both sides of paper'). Present with 1-2 sentences per rule.
rw: Reading and writing slot: 'KET-style Gap Fill' - Students read a short text about Earth Day and fill in 5 gaps with must/should. Then write 2 sentences about their own green habits.
st: Story: 'The Earth Day Hero' - Read a short story about a teen who makes green changes. End with the goodbye routine: 'Today we reviewed must/should for green rules. Thanks for your hard work!'
g: Teams race to answer Earth Day questions for points.
Students draw Earth Day words for teams to guess.
Teams sort cards into 'must' and 'should' categories.
Students act out green actions for teams to shout.
diff: Fast finishers: Add a sixth rule with a 'must not' (e.g., 'You must not litter').
Support: Provide sentence starters (e.g., 'You must...') for the poster.
hw: Homework 1: Design a 5-rule green poster for your home using must/should.
Homework 2: Write 5 sentences about what you must/should do to help the planet.
Homework 3: Interview a family member about their green habits and report back.
tip: Use local examples (e.g., 'You should save water in Oujda') to make the rules relevant and memorable.
